references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, Joshua gives the command to take twelve stones from the Jordan, paralleling the twelve stones that were set up in the river.
The twelve stones taken from the Jordan were set up at Gilgal as a memorial, an action parallel to the stones raised in the river.
The priests who carried the ark of the covenant stood still in the middle of the Jordan while the people crossed over, at that same place where Joshua set up the stones.
Jacob set up a stone as a memorial at Bethel, a similar practice of raising stones to remember God's intervention.
Samuel set up a stone and called it Ebenezer as a memorial, similar to Joshua's action of setting up stones in remembrance.
The stones were to be an everlasting memorial for the children of Israel about how the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant.
